acceptance: A merge-blocking review path exists that does not depend on Codex connector availability
Documented in the review protocol which fallback applies and who can invoke it
context:
On 2026-10-06 PR #2721 (portable metadata store) was blocked: the Codex connector posted a usage-limit notice instead of a review, and oracle-review accepts only its review or a stand-in attestation from a listed attester (joeharris76). The only unblock path required the owner personally. Observed during the tuning-followups batch.
2026-10-08: a second failure mode. On PR #2751, `@codex review` comments at 21:23 and about 22:05 UTC got no response at all: no review, no limit notice, no reaction. The connector last reviewed that PR on 2026-10-07 (a78cdb8db). The PR was a draft at the first request; it was ready at the second. A silent connector is harder to detect than a limit notice, so the fallback should also cover "no response within N minutes".
2026-10-08, third occurrence: PR #2781 (Polars engine option, soundness path) got three `@codex review` requests (16:02Z, 16:43Z, 18:46Z) and no response of any kind for over 4 hours; no other open PR (#2775, #2776, #2777, #2780, #2782) had connector activity either. The connector's last review was 2026-10-08 05:47Z. The PR sat unmergeable until the owner approved a stand-in review (20:53Z); the batch it belonged to was blocked for about 4 hours, and the oracle-review failure text gave no sign that the connector was unresponsive rather than slow.
2026-10-09 (closeout): resolved by the oracle cutover, not by the feat/oracle-review-app-fallbacks branch. Since #2758 (96c26ad3c) the required oracle-review check passes on the benchbox-oracle app's success review of the current head, which runs on every head and does not depend on the Codex connector; the stand-in attestation by a listed attester remains the backup. docs/operations/merge-queue-governance.md (Soundness Review Boundary and the oracle-review row) records which signal applies and who can attest. The branch (16c4ba79) added claude-review and Gemini fallbacks and retired the stand-in marker; a rebase had 29 conflict hunks in the merge gate and the design is superseded. The owner chose to discard it. Recovery ref: refs/tbh/recovery/before-discard/20261009T010500Z-feat-oracle-review-app-fallbacks.
description: Decide and document a fallback when the Codex connector is at its usage limit: e.g. limit monitoring/alerting before it blocks merges, a second eligible reviewer, or widening stand-in attester rules. Goal is that no PR sits unmergeable waiting on an external quota reset.
